external_entities.name: admin
external_entities.description: A person who maintains the database directly.
external_entities.source_excerpt: There is an admin who maintains the database directly
external_entities.notes: The admin's location is unspecified: they do it from wherever they happen to be.

external_entities.name: CDN
external_entities.description: The content delivery network from which readers fetch published assets.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Readers fetch those from the CDN over HTTP.

processes.name: web server

processes.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS and keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database

processes.name: CMS
processes.description: The content management system running on the web server.

data_stores.name: MySQL database

data_stores.source_excerpt: keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database on the same hosted network

data_flows.data_description: site pages, account interactions, and comments

data_flows.name: fetch assets
data_flows.description: Readers fetch images, stylesheets, and downloads from the CDN.

data_flows.name: publish assets
data_flows.description: The web server pushes newly published assets to the CDN bucket.

data_flows.data_description: newly published images, stylesheets and downloads

data_flows.description: The web server keeps pages, accounts, and comments in the MySQL database.

data_flows.name: database maintenance
data_flows.description: The admin maintains the database directly rather than through the CMS.
data_flows.source_excerpt: There is an admin who maintains the database directly rather than through the CMS.

trust_boundaries.name: hosted network

assumptions.assumption: The web server is internet-facing because it serves the public site that readers access.
assumptions.basis: The source calls it a public site and says readers hit the web server over HTTPS.

assumptions.assumption: The MySQL database is confidential because it holds accounts and comments in addition to site pages.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the database contains pages, accounts and comments; accounts and comments can identify or describe people.

assumptions.assumption: The CDN bucket's contents are public because readers fetch the published assets from the CDN.
assumptions.basis: The source says readers fetch the images, stylesheets, and downloads from the CDN, and that the web server pushes new assets to the CDN bucket.
